questions.q: In the EC2 instance type `m5.large`, what does each part represent?
options: m = family (general purpose), 5 = generation, large = size
m = Region code, 5 = number of vCPUs, large = storage capacity
m = pricing model, 5 = number of Availability Zones, large = network bandwidth
The instance type string has no structured meaning
questions.explain: Instance types are consistently structured as family + generation + size, e.g. m5.large = general purpose, 5th generation, large size.

questions.q: What is the tradeoff of using EC2 Spot Instances?
options: Steep discounts on spare AWS capacity, but AWS can reclaim the instance on short notice
Guaranteed capacity forever at the highest possible price
No discount at all compared to On-Demand pricing
Spot Instances require a mandatory 3-year commitment
questions.explain: Spot trades reliability (AWS can reclaim capacity) for a steep discount versus On-Demand pricing.

questions.q: How does Lambda's billing model fundamentally differ from EC2's?
options: Lambda bills per invocation and execution duration, with nothing charged while idle; EC2 bills for the instance running, whether busy or idle
Lambda and EC2 use identical hourly billing models
Lambda requires a fixed monthly subscription regardless of usage
EC2 only bills when the instance is idle, not when it's actively processing
questions.explain: Lambda's pay-per-invocation model with no idle cost is what makes it fundamentally different from an always-running EC2 instance.

questions.q: Why does Lambda fit a short, event-triggered task (like reacting to a new S3 file) better than a permanently running EC2 instance?
options: Lambda runs only when triggered and costs nothing while idle, matching the bursty, on-demand nature of the task
Lambda functions can run for an unlimited amount of time per invocation
EC2 instances cannot be triggered by S3 events under any configuration
Lambda is always cheaper than EC2 for every possible workload
questions.explain: The event-driven, short-duration billing model is exactly what makes Lambda a natural fit for reactive, on-trigger tasks.

questions.q: What EC2 instance family would best fit a CPU-heavy compute workload, per this lesson?
options: The c family (compute-optimized)
The r family (memory-optimized)
The t family (burstable general purpose)
There is no family distinction for different workload shapes
questions.explain: The c family is explicitly called out as built for CPU-heavy workloads, as opposed to r (memory) or t (bursty) families.
